name: United Arab Emirates
genZNote: Seven emirates, one federation, one very large Indian diaspora — the UAE and Gujarat have been trading partners since long before 'Vibrant Gujarat' was a summit name.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located on the Arabian Peninsula, bordering Saudi Arabia and Oman, along the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman.
A federation of seven emirates: Abu Dhabi (capital), Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Fujairah, and Ras Al Khaimah.
Mostly desert terrain, with major coastal cities built up through rapid modern development.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Arabic is the official language; English is widely used in business given the country's large expatriate population.

Emiratis are a minority within their own country — the UAE has one of the world's highest expatriate-to-citizen population ratios, with a very large Indian community, including many from Gujarat and Kerala.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federation of seven absolute monarchies (emirates), each ruled by its own Emir; the President is traditionally the Ruler of Abu Dhabi.
Formed in 1971 when six emirates federated (Ras Al Khaimah joined in 1972) after the end of British protection treaties.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Member of the United Nations, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
Hosted the COP28 UN Climate Change Conference in Dubai (2023), a notable recent global-diplomacy moment.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: The UAE is one of India's largest trading partners, and India-UAE signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) that came into force in 2022.
Home to one of the largest overseas Indian communities in the world, with especially strong Gujarati- and Kerala-origin populations in Dubai and Sharjah.
Significant remittance flows from Indian workers in the UAE form an important part of bilateral economic ties.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Historically built on oil and gas exports; has diversified heavily into trade, tourism, aviation (Dubai and Abu Dhabi as major hubs), finance, and real estate.
Dubai is a major global re-export and logistics hub connecting Asia, Europe, and Africa.
A significant destination for Indian exports and a source of crude oil imports for India.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The Burj Khalifa (world's tallest building) in Dubai, rapid modern urban development, and being a major global aviation/trade hub.
A large Indian diaspora and close economic ties with India via the CEPA trade agreement.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: UAE Dirham (AED), pegged to the US Dollar.
Built on oil wealth, now diversified into finance, tourism, aviation, and trade; Dubai is a major global logistics and business hub.
Home to some of the world's tallest buildings and largest ports and airports.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Predominantly arid desert terrain with a Persian Gulf coastline; relies heavily on desalination for freshwater.
Pursuing large-scale renewable-energy and afforestation projects as part of economic diversification.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Formed in 1971 as a federation of seven emirates (including Abu Dhabi and Dubai) after independence from British protection.
Transformed rapidly from a modest trading and pearling economy into a global business hub following oil discoveries.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1971 founding of the federation of seven emirates.
A federal system with each emirate retaining significant autonomy; governed by a Supreme Council of Rulers, with the President traditionally from Abu Dhabi.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: UAE Space Agency achieved a landmark with the Hope Probe reaching Mars orbit in 2021, making the UAE the first Arab nation to reach Mars.
Home to ambitious futuristic infrastructure projects and a growing renewable-energy sector.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Hosts major international sporting and business events, including Formula 1 and global expos (Expo 2020 Dubai).
The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the world's tallest building.
The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi is an internationally recognised architectural landmark.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and OPEC.
Member of the UN and the Arab League; increasingly active in global diplomacy and trade partnerships.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The UAE is a federation of seven emirates on the Arabian Peninsula, formed in 1971, and one of India's largest trading partners.
keyFacts: Capital: Abu Dhabi. Currency: UAE Dirham.
Federation formed: 1971 (six emirates; Ras Al Khaimah joined 1972).
India-UAE CEPA trade agreement came into force in 2022.
Home to one of the world's largest overseas Indian communities.
commonConfusion: Abu Dhabi is the UAE's CAPITAL; Dubai is its largest and most internationally famous city — the two are often mixed up.

highYieldFacts: UAE = 7 emirates, federated in 1971; Abu Dhabi is the capital, not Dubai.
India-UAE CEPA came into force in 2022 — a frequently tested trade-agreement fact.
commonTraps: Naming Dubai as the UAE's capital instead of Abu Dhabi.
mustRemember: UAE formed in 1971 from 7 emirates; large Indian/Gujarati diaspora; CEPA with India since 2022.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-UAE Relations
